source_title: Domino's Pizza, Inc. - Form 10-K (Fiscal Year Ended January 3, 2016)
publisher_issuer: Domino's Pizza, Inc. (filed with U.S. SEC, EDGAR CIK 0001286681, accession 0001193125-16-476935)
company_context: Following its 2009-2010 'Pizza Turnaround' relaunch (reformulated recipe plus a self-critical marketing campaign) and a sustained investment in digital ordering technology, Domino's compounded years of comparable-sales growth. This record focuses on the SUSTAINED multi-year growth in fiscal 2015, well after the relaunch, rather than the 2010 relaunch event itself.
business_type: Quick-service pizza franchisor (QSR; predominantly franchised, technology-led ordering)
geography: United States and international (master-franchise model abroad)
macro_context: Rapid shift to digital/mobile food ordering and delivery; competitive QSR pizza category; Domino's positioning as a 'technology company that sells pizza' driving order frequency and ticket.
evidence_summary: Domino's converted its post-relaunch product and digital investments into sustained, compounding comparable-sales growth. For fiscal 2015, domestic same-store sales grew 12.0% for the full year (and 10.7% in the fourth quarter year over year), while international same-store sales grew 7.8% for the full year (8.6% in Q4). The fourth quarter marked the 88th consecutive quarter (22nd full year) of positive international same-store sales growth, evidence that the improvement was durable and multi-year rather than a one-time relaunch bump.

source_backed_metrics.consecutive_quarters_positive_internatio: 88 (22nd consecutive full year, as of Q4 fiscal 2015)

owner_decision_context: Management sustained the strategy that followed the 2010 relaunch: continued product/quality credibility plus heavy, ongoing investment in proprietary digital ordering and loyalty, prioritizing order frequency and convenience to keep compounding comparable sales rather than treating the relaunch as a finished project.
action_taken: Continued investment in digital ordering platforms, loyalty, and operational execution across the franchised network, sustaining high single-to-double-digit comparable-sales growth domestically and internationally.
outcome_evidence: FY2015 domestic same-store sales up 12.0% and international up 7.8%, with the 88th consecutive quarter of positive international comps, confirm durable multi-year improvement well beyond the 2010 relaunch.
